definition: An API is a set of rules that allows two software applications to communicate.
An array is a data structure that stores multiple values in a single variable.
A function is a reusable block of code that performs a task.
A variable is a named place used to store or refer to a value.
A loop repeats a block of code while a condition is met or for each item in a collection.
A data type that can only have one of two values, typically true or false.
A sequence of characters used to represent text in a program.
A numeric data type that represents whole numbers without a fractional component.
A data type that represents numbers with a decimal point or fractional part.
A collection of key-value pairs representing data and behavior in object-oriented programming.
A blueprint or template for creating objects with defined properties and methods.
A function that is associated with an object or a class.
A mechanism where a class can inherit properties and methods from another class.
The ability of different classes to respond to the same method call in unique ways.
Bundling data and methods that operate on that data within one unit and restricting direct access.
A programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a smaller piece of the same problem.
A finite set of well-defined instructions to solve a specific problem or perform a computation.
A mathematical notation used to describe the performance or complexity of an algorithm.
An organized collection of structured data or information stored electronically in a computer system.
A standard programming language used for managing and querying relational databases.
A database designed to store and retrieve data in formats other than traditional relational tables.
A column or set of columns in a database table that uniquely identifies each row.
A column or group of columns in a table that links to the primary key of another table.
A data structure that improves the speed of data retrieval operations on a database table.
A technique that lets you query and manipulate data from a database using an object-oriented paradigm.
A lightweight data-interchange format that is easy for humans to read and write and machines to parse.
An architectural style for designing networked applications using standard HTTP methods.
A query language for APIs that lets clients request exact data they need.
A cross-platform and language-independent interface that treats an XML or HTML document as a tree structure.
The standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
A style sheet language used for describing the presentation of a document written in HTML.
A distributed version control system for tracking changes in source code during software development.
A web-based platform used for version control and collaboration using Git.
A storage location where source code and files are managed and version-tracked.
An operation that sends the latest changes of the source code to the repository history.
A parallel version of a repository that lets you work without affecting the main line.
Combining changes from multiple divergent branches of source code into a single branch.
A set of platform-as-a-service products that use OS-level virtualization to deliver software in containers.
A standard unit of software that packages up code and all its dependencies so the application runs quickly.
An open-source system for automating deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications.
A numerical label assigned to each device connected to a computer network.
A hierarchical decentralized naming system for computers or services connected to the Internet.
An application layer protocol for distributed, collaborative, hypermedia information systems.
An extension of HTTP used for secure communication over a computer network.
Cryptographic protocols designed to provide communications security over a computer network.
A hardware or software component that stores data so future requests for that data can be served faster.
A small piece of data sent from a website and stored on the user's computer by the web browser.
A string of data that represents credentials or permissions to access a resource or service.
The process of verifying the identity of a user, process, or device.
The function of specifying access rights and privileges to resources.
A method to frequently deliver apps to customers by introducing automation into the stages of app development.
A software application that provides comprehensive facilities to computer programmers for software development.
A computer program that translates computer code written in one programming language into another language.
A computer program that directly executes instructions written in a programming or scripting language without prior compilation.
A linear data structure that follows the Last In, First Out principle.
A linear data structure that follows the First In, First Out principle.
A tree data structure in which each node has at most two children.
A data structure that implements an associative array abstract data type, a structure that can map keys to values.
A state in which each member of a group is waiting for another member to take action, such as releasing a lock.
An architectural style that structures an application as a collection of loosely coupled services.
A software application in which all functional components are combined into a single program on a single platform.
A way for an app to provide other applications with real-time information via an HTTP POST payload.
